sections.html:
Gables owners tend to weigh three paths: a broker listing, a for-sale-by-owner attempt, or a direct purchase by someone paying cash with the house untouched. The calendar and the condition of the roof, kitchen and systems decide most cases.

The local wrinkle is history. More than 1,000 properties appear on the Coral Gables Register of Historic Places, and if yours could be among them, call the city before a buyer hears any renovation promise from you. At $2,373 a month, typical rent is high enough that some owners wonder about keeping the house as a rental, but that brings landlord duties of its own.

Coral Gables is a Miami-Dade County city of 49,578 people, and owners live in 64.5% of its homes. The typical owned home is worth $1,089,900, so a pricing opinion on your own block matters more than any citywide number.

Plenty of Gables buyers relocate from overseas or other states. Offering a translated summary of the terms helps, and so does a neat title file, since distant buyers generally want a smooth, fast closing.

The city's permits page lists every permit it issues, and the City Services Directory covers anything you cannot find there. Building staff can tell you whether any permit on your address was never closed out. Better to hear that from them this week than from a buyer's title agent mid-contract.

The Development and City Projects page tracks traffic calming and large construction, so scan it for work planned near your block. Agendas and public notices are posted under City Meetings.

Miami-Dade charges 60 cents for every $100 on a deed. The county adds a 45 cents per $100 surtax too, though a transfer of nothing but a single-family house escapes it. You can read the base rate in s. 201.02, and anyone whose name is on the document can be held responsible for it, regardless of what your contract assigns.

  • The clerk takes payment the moment the deed is filed.
  • Recording runs $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each after it (section 28.24), plus trust fund and technology charges.
  • Two people must witness your signature (section 689.01).

An itemized closing statement lets you check every one of these charges ahead of signing day.

Someone buying a Gables homestead you have held for decades can face a much bigger bill than yours, since the sale pushes assessed value up to just value.

  • Save Our Homes limits annual increases to 3 percent or the inflation figure, whichever is smaller.
  • Up to $50,000 comes off taxable value under homestead, with a March 1 filing date.
  • Leasing the house to a tenant ends the exemption.

Billing is the tax collector's job, not the appraiser's, and paying in November earns a discount that starts at 4 percent. Assessment questions can go to the Miami-Dade appraiser's public line, 305-375-4712.

sections.h2: If the house has a mortgage default, a tenant or an estate
sections.html:
Three situations, three separate timetables. Following a foreclosure judgment, the court auction is set 20 to 35 days later, so closing privately beforehand may save the equity you hold. If an estate is selling, the personal representative's deed is listed as non-taxable.

  • Small estates, meaning $150,000 or less of non-exempt property, can take the summary route in s. 735.201.
  • A month-to-month tenancy ends on 30 days' notice (s. 83.57).
  • Missed rent begins with a written demand giving 3 days.

A free Clerk of Court alert warns you when a deed or mortgage is recorded in your name, which helps if the house sits empty or came to you by inheritance.

sections.h2: Steps after you accept an offer
sections.html:
After you say yes, the deed is drafted, signed in front of two witnesses and recorded by the Miami-Dade clerk. Audio-video witnessing is allowed, which lets an owner in another state sign from home.

  1. Request a payoff statement from your lender and collect permit records.
  2. Find out whether your homestead status stops at closing.
  3. Have the title agent explain the split of this year's tax bill.
  4. Read the settlement statement slowly the day before.
  5. File away your copy of the recorded deed.

Planning to buy again in Florida? The portability form goes in alongside the application for the new homestead.

Relief for older owners and for veteran owners rides on the homestead, so it stops when you sell. The Miami-Dade appraiser lets owners file widow and veteran disability exemptions online.

  • A veteran over 65 with a permanent service-connected disability can receive a homestead discount equal to the VA rating.
  • Tax deferral requests are due at the tax collector by March 31.

Holding one of these? Ask the appraiser how it is treated at closing and whether it can be claimed on your next home.

Cash removes the lender from the picture. No appraisal, no underwriting queue, no repair list handed down by a loan officer. Title still has to be clean, though, so liens, unpaid code charges and open permits get settled before or at the closing table.

That suits a house with postponed maintenance, a tenant living in it, or a seller racing a move date. If the place is in good condition and you have time, a retail buyer may bring a better price. Collect at least two offers and ask each buyer for proof of funds and a written closing date.

Bring photo ID, keys, garage openers and any warranty papers to closing. The title company shows you where to sign, and your proceeds arrive by wire or check once the deed is recorded.

Preparation trims days off almost any sale. Put the deed, the newest tax bill, a lender payoff figure and permit records in one folder. When heirs or co-owners are involved, settle early who has the authority to sign.

Judge each offer by what lands in your account, how long closing takes and how likely the buyer is to back out. A listing exposes the house to more people but brings showings and financing conditions. Whoever you pick, get in writing who covers title, recording and deed tax. If a buyer asks for a longer inspection window or a lower price after the first walk-through, decide ahead of time what you would accept, so a rushed moment does not make the decision for you. Keep every message with a buyer in one place in case a question comes up later.

faqs.q: How much is a typical Coral Gables house worth?
faqs.a: The typical owned-home value is $1,089,900 for 2020-2024. Your own house could land well above or below that.

faqs.q: Does a historic designation affect my sale?
faqs.a: It can, if the house is on the city's historic register. Ask city staff about your address before you promise a buyer any renovation.

faqs.q: Who pays documentary stamp tax on a Coral Gables deed?
faqs.a: Whoever the contract names, though everyone on the deed shares liability. The surtax skips a document moving only a single-family dwelling.

faqs.q: Will my property taxes follow me to a new home?
faqs.a: Partly. Portability can move some homestead savings to a new Florida home if you qualify, using Form DR-501T.

faqs.q: Where do I ask about my assessment?
faqs.a: Call the Miami-Dade appraiser's public line at 305-375-4712 or book an appointment through the appraiser's website.
